subject: Cloud Computing
title: Edge Computing and Data
description: A 60-second lesson on Edge Computing and Data.

hook.text: A self-driving car generates 4 TB of data per day. Sending it all to the cloud is too slow. Process it at the edge.

buildup.text: Edge computing processes data close to where it's created: in factories, cell towers, stores, and vehicles.

discovery.text: AWS Outposts, Azure Stack, and Google Distributed Cloud bring cloud services to locations outside data centers.

twist.text: Edge doesn't replace the cloud — it extends it. Critical decisions happen locally; everything else syncs to the cloud.

climax.text: As IoT grows, more data will be processed at the edge than in centralized clouds. The shift has already begun.

punchline.text: Some data can't wait for the cloud. Edge processes it locally.

quiz.question: Why is edge computing necessary for self-driving cars?
options: The massive data volume and latency requirements demand local processing
Self-driving cars cannot connect to the internet
Cloud providers do not allow automotive data on their servers

details.summary: Edge computing processes data near its source instead of sending everything to a central cloud. This reduces latency, saves bandwidth, and enables real-time decisions for IoT, autonomous vehicles, and industrial applications where milliseconds matter.
details.whyItMatters: Not all data can or should travel to the cloud. Edge computing extends cloud capabilities to locations where latency, bandwidth, or data sovereignty require local processing.
takeaways: Data is processed near its source for minimal latency
Reduces bandwidth costs by filtering data before cloud upload
Essential for IoT, autonomous systems, and real-time control

faq.question: How does edge computing relate to cloud computing?
faq.answer: Edge computing extends the cloud rather than replacing it. Time-sensitive processing happens at the edge for speed, while the cloud handles aggregation, training ML models, and long-term storage. Most architectures use both in a complementary hybrid approach.

faq.question: What hardware runs at the edge?
faq.answer: Edge devices range from small IoT gateways and Raspberry Pis to rack-mounted servers in telecom towers. AWS Outposts and Azure Stack bring full cloud services to edge locations. The hardware depends on the processing demands of the workload.
